# REPORT.md structure (generated by `xpu-report make`, finished by you)

Sections: title + setup (hardware, profiler, candidate, profiles) / 0 Profiling setup (harness, cases, caveats) / 1 Headline numbers (table per profile + one-line read) / 2 Per-dimension findings (launch geometry & waves, balance/tail, stalls, tensor, memory/spills) / 3 Summary diagnosis table / 4 Optimization directions: **3-5 priorities**, each with
- the change, concretely (file/function/config key),
- **Evidence:** metric values and rule hits,
- **Expected impact:** % on which op/case (your estimate, overruling the script's upper bound when warranted),
- **Effort:** low/medium/high + what is edited,
- **Why now:** why this ranks above the next one,
- **Wiki:** page ids /
5 Confidence & caveats / 6 Reproduction commands.

Style rules
- Cite specific numbers for every claim. "SBID 35%, XMX 34%" beats "stalls are high".
- Name config keys and functions (`k_grouped.prefetch`, `gemm_tile`, `Scheduler::locate`).
- Rank by magnitude; stop at 5; do not pad.
- State when you overrule a script heuristic and why.
- Link artifacts (profile text files, JOB dirs).
Anti-patterns: generic advice without evidence; repeating the same profile under different tags; reporting straight from the CLI table; omitting the setup/reproduction.
